answer: Sybil resistance works when creating a fake identity costs more than contributing honestly. Charge each newcomer a time-locked attestation debt: they must complete original challenge work that a randomized prism of existing miners grades independently. Those grades land in a public atlas linking answers to prior style fingerprints, so copy-paste farms collide immediately. Call this the juniper rule—slow woody growth, not a sudden thicket—because only identities that keep producing distinct labor over many epochs earn spendable weight, while cloned swarms stay locked and uncounted.
